summary: This lecture continues after Taif: the Prophet SAW prayed at Nakhla at night and a group of jinn believed, then he re-entered Mecca under the protection of Mut'im ibn Adi. The ustaz then begins the Isra' and Mi'raj. Jibril split his chest at Hijr Ismail and filled it with faith and wisdom, he rode the Buraq to Jerusalem, led the prophets in prayer, and ascended through the seven heavens. At each he was greeted by prophets: Adam, Isa and Yahya, Yusuf, Idris, Harun, Musa who wept because his followers would be more numerous in paradise, and Ibrahim who leaned on al-Bayt al-Ma'mur and conveyed his greeting and four dhikr as plants of paradise. The gifts from Allah continue next class.
keyPoints: On the way back from Taif, the Prophet SAW prayed at night at Nakhla and a group of jinn heard the Quran and believed.
Mut'im ibn Adi gave protection and escorted the Prophet SAW back into Mecca.
The Isra' began when Jibril opened the roof, split his chest and filled it with faith and wisdom.
The Prophet SAW rode the Buraq to Jerusalem, led the prophets in prayer, then ascended through seven heavens meeting the prophets.
Ibrahim conveyed his greeting to this ummah and taught four dhikr that become plants in paradise.

chapters.title: Opening and the two-month break
chapters.summary: The ustaz says the Isra' and Mi'raj is hard to believe but must be believed, and chats about the Independence Day performances.

chapters.title: The jinn at Nakhla
chapters.summary: After Taif, the Prophet SAW prayed at night at Nakhla and a group of jinn listened silently, then returned to preach to their people.

chapters.title: The cut passport and Mut'im
chapters.summary: Zaid worried about re-entering Mecca. Mut'im ibn Adi gave jiwar and Abu Jahal had to respect it.

chapters.title: Pressure in Mecca and the start of Isra' Mi'raj
chapters.summary: After Khadijah and Abu Talib died, Quraysh harmed the Prophet SAW. One night his roof opened and Jibril descended.

chapters.title: The first verse of Surah Al-Isra'
chapters.summary: The ustaz explains that Subhana signals what is beyond reason and links the blessing of al-Aqsa with prayer for Palestine.

chapters.title: The chest is opened at Hijr Ismail
chapters.summary: He lay in the Hijr, his chest was opened and his heart washed with zamzam, then filled with faith and wisdom from a golden vessel.

chapters.title: The Buraq
chapters.summary: The white Buraq, like a horse, balked, then sweated from shame at the Prophet's honour.

chapters.title: Jerusalem and prayer with the prophets
chapters.summary: The Buraq strode as far as the eye could see. At al-Aqsa he led 124,000 prophets in prayer.

chapters.title: The seven heavens and Adam
chapters.summary: Each heaven has a gate and a prophet to greet him. In the first heaven Adam welcomed his righteous son.

chapters.title: Isa, Yahya and the vastness of the heavens
chapters.summary: In the second heaven he met Isa and Yahya in matching clothes. The ustaz shows how vast the first heaven is.

chapters.title: Yusuf and Idris
chapters.summary: Yusuf in the third heaven had half of beauty. Idris in the fourth was the first to write with a pen.

chapters.title: Harun, the gatekeepers and Musa
chapters.summary: Harun in the fifth heaven, Musa in the sixth wept because the Prophet's followers would be more numerous in paradise.

chapters.title: Ibrahim and al-Bayt al-Ma'mur
chapters.summary: Ibrahim leaned on al-Bayt al-Ma'mur, called him son, conveyed his greeting and taught four dhikr. The ustaz ties it to the Ibrahimiyya salawat.

chapters.title: Allah's gifts and other sights
chapters.summary: The ustaz previews the special gifts, the scent of Mashita, the punished, and Bilal's footsteps in paradise for next class.

chapters.title: Recap in question form
chapters.summary: The ustaz reviews from Nakhla, Mut'im's jiwar, the chest operation, the Buraq to the order of prophets in the seven heavens.

chapters.title: Q&A: al-Aqsa and the qiblat
chapters.summary: The ustaz answers questions on al-Aqsa having no building then, Yusuf, why the ascent was from Jerusalem, and the first qiblat.

dalil.context: The ustaz mentions Prophet Yunus's supplication taught for those in hardship.
dalil.translation: And remember the man with the whale,when he went off angrily, thinking We could not restrict him, but then he cried out in the deep darkness, ‘There is no God but You, glory be to You, I was wrong.’

dalil.context: Allah tells of a group of jinn turned toward the Prophet SAW to hear the Quran.
dalil.translation: We sent a group of jinn to you [Prophet] to listen to the Quran. When they heard it, they said to one another, ‘Be quiet!’ Then when it was finished they turned to their community and gave them warning.

dalil.context: The jinn told their people they had heard a book sent down after Musa.
dalil.translation: They said, ‘Our people, we have been listening to a Scripture that came after Moses, confirming previous scriptures, giving guidance to the truth and the straight path.

dalil.context: Allah told the Prophet SAW to announce that a group of jinn heard a wondrous Quran.
dalil.translation: Say [Prophet], ‘It has been revealed to me that a group of jinn once listened in and said, “We have heard a wondrous Quran,

dalil.context: Allah took His servant by night from al-Masjid al-Haram to al-Masjid al-Aqsa whose surroundings He blessed.
dalil.translation: Glory to Him who made His servant travel by night from the sacred place of worship to the furthest place of worship, whose surroundings We have blessed, to show him some of Our signs: He alone is the All Hearing, the All Seeing.

dalil.context: The ustaz cites that Allah adorned the lowest heaven with stars, to show how vast the first heaven is.
dalil.translation: We have adorned the lowest heaven with lamps and made them [missiles] for stoning devils for whom We have also prepared the torment of a blazing fire.

dalil.context: Allah says We raised him to a high station, linked to Idris.
dalil.translation: We raised him to a high position.
The Prophet SAW said his roof opened while he was in Mecca, Jibril descended, split his chest, washed it with zamzam and filled it with faith and wisdom from a golden vessel.
dalil.context: The ustaz recounts this long hadith and says it is mentioned among others by Bukhari. He does not name the narrator.

dalil.translation: The Buraq was brought fully bridled and saddled. When Jibril rebuked it, it was ashamed and sweated, for none was more honoured by Allah than the Prophet SAW.
dalil.context: The ustaz narrates the hadith of the Buraq. He does not name a narrator or source.

dalil.translation: Jibril introduced the prophets in each heaven and they welcomed the Prophet SAW with greetings: Adam, Isa and Yahya, Yusuf, Idris, Harun, Musa and Ibrahim.
dalil.context: The ustaz relays the order of the prophets from the hadith. He names no narrator or source, except the Idris account which he attributes to Sahih Muslim.

dalil.translation: Musa wept because a young man sent after him would have more followers entering paradise than his own.
dalil.context: The ustaz narrates Musa's reply. He does not name a narrator or source.

dalil.translation: Ibrahim said: O Muhammad, convey my greeting to your ummah and tell them paradise has fertile soil, sweet water and its plants are Subhanallah, Alhamdulillah, La ilaha illallah, Allahu akbar.
dalil.context: The ustaz relays Ibrahim's message. He does not name a narrator or source.

dalil.translation: Every day seventy thousand angels enter al-Bayt al-Ma'mur and do not return.
dalil.context: The ustaz relays this report. He does not name a narrator or source.

people.context: Escorted the Prophet SAW into Mecca with his sons and died before Badr.

people.role: One who refused to grant protection
people.context: Refused the Prophet's request for protection.
Worried about how to re-enter Mecca.
Asked Mut'im whether he was protecting or following the Prophet SAW.
Welcomed him as righteous son and rejoiced at righteous people.
With Yahya, cousins, in matching clothes; not yet deceased.
Cousin of Isa who greeted him as a brother.
The first to write with a pen, raised by Allah to a high station.
Musa's brother who greeted him as a brother.
Wept because Muhammad's ummah would be more numerous in paradise.
Leaned on al-Bayt al-Ma'mur, conveying a greeting and four dhikr.
Opened his chest, brought the Buraq and answered the gatekeepers.
His footsteps were heard in paradise; the story continues next class.
Named as the one whose faith was never shaken.

sirah.era: After Taif: the Isra' and Mi'raj
sirah.summary: This lecture covers the jinn at Nakhla, Mut'im's protection and the Isra' Mi'raj up to meeting Ibrahim.

events.label: Nakhla
events.title: Jinn hear the Quran
events.desc: They believed and returned to preach to their people.

events.label: Protection
events.title: Mut'im grants protection
events.desc: He entered Mecca escorted by Mut'im's sons.

events.label: Isra'
events.title: The chest is opened
events.desc: Jibril washed the heart with zamzam and filled it with faith and wisdom.

events.label: Buraq
events.title: Riding the Buraq
events.desc: He was carried to Jerusalem in an instant.

events.label: Mi'raj
events.title: Ascent to the seven heavens
events.desc: Each heaven has a gate, a gatekeeper and a prophet.

events.label: Ibrahim
events.title: Meeting Ibrahim
events.desc: He received a greeting and the dhikr that plant paradise.

lessons.title: Believing what is beyond reason
lessons.body: The Isra' Mi'raj is hard to grasp by logic but Allah narrated it, so we must believe.

lessons.title: Silence and respect for Quran recitation
lessons.body: The jinn stopped and listened silently; we should not joke while the Quran is recited.

lessons.title: Awe at the Quran's beauty
lessons.body: The jinn marvelled at the Quran's language, rhythm and meaning.

lessons.title: Valuing help even from non-Muslims
lessons.body: The Prophet SAW remembered Mut'im and was ready to free the Badr captives for him.

lessons.title: Allah strengthens His Messenger
lessons.body: After the grief of Taif, Allah took him to witness a grand realm.

lessons.title: Using Yunus's prayer in hardship
lessons.body: Yunus's prayer is recited by those in hardship.

lessons.title: Do not stall with questions when told to act
lessons.body: Bani Israil asked many questions because they did not want to carry out the command.

lessons.title: Answering Ibrahim's greeting with salawat
lessons.body: In prayer we recite the Ibrahimiyya salawat as a reply to his greeting.

lessons.title: Dhikr plants trees in paradise
lessons.body: Subhanallah, Alhamdulillah, La ilaha illallah and Allahu akbar become plants in paradise.

lessons.title: Praying for Palestine
lessons.body: Al-Aqsa is blessed and we pray for the liberation of Jerusalem and Gaza.

glossary.meaning: The Prophet's night journey from Mecca to Jerusalem.
The Prophet's ascent from Jerusalem to the heavens.
The white mount, smaller than a horse, that carried the Prophet SAW.
Protection granted by a leader to another.
The highest station where the Prophet SAW met Allah.
The Kaaba of the seventh heaven where seventy thousand angels circumambulate daily.
The salawat in the final tashahhud that mentions Ibrahim.
The semicircular area beside the Kaaba.
